shortDescription: Sweden's Vattenfall said on Thursday it will build a large battery storage facility in Germany after taking a final investment decision for the project.

children: Sweden's Vattenfall said on Thursday it will build a large battery storage facility in Germany after taking a final investment decision for the project.
The project will be built on the site of the former Brunsbuttel nuclear power plant, which is currently being decommissioned, Vattenfall said in a statement.
"Demand for battery storage is rising rapidly as renewable generation expands," it added.
The battery and the connection to the grid is expected to be operational by the end of 2028.
It has an output of 254 megawatts (MW) and a storage capacity of around 1,000 MWh, which is one of Germany's largest battery storage projects, according to Vattenfall.
The company did not say how much money it would invest in the project.
